title: Roasted Beetroot Salad
subtitle: sweet roasted beetroot with feta, walnuts, and thyme
excerpt: Roasting beetroot concentrates its natural sweetness and gives a better flavour than boiling. This salad pairs it with crumbled feta, crunchy walnuts, and a sharp lemon dressing. It works as a starter, a side, or a light lunch.
sourceNotes: Roasted beetroot salad is found across British, Scandinavian, and Eastern European cooking. The combination of beetroot and goat's cheese or feta became popular in British restaurants in the 1990s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the beetroot up to 2 days ahead and keep in the fridge.

content.text: Wear gloves when handling raw beetroot -- the juice stains. Wrapping the beetroot in foil to roast is optional but keeps moisture in. You can also roast them unwrapped for a slightly more caramelised result.

items.prepNote: use 2 small red onions, cut into wedges

content.text: Preheat the oven to 200C. Toss the beetroot and red onion wedges with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and the thyme. Season with salt. Spread in a roasting tin.
Roast for 45 to 50 minutes until the beetroot is tender when pierced with a knife. Cool slightly.
Peel the beetroot when cool enough to handle. Slice or quarter.
Whisk together the remaining olive oil, lemon juice, and honey to make the dressing.
Arrange the beetroot and onion on a platter. Scatter over the feta and walnuts. Drizzle with the dressing. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: Beetroot is still hard after 50 minutes
items.cause: Beetroot is very large or oven temperature too low
items.fix: Cut large beetroot in half before roasting. Check oven temperature with a thermometer.
Roast until very tender -- the skin should slip off easily.

content.text: Beetroot salads are common across Britain, Scandinavia, and Eastern Europe, where beetroot has been a winter staple for centuries. The British version pairing roasted beetroot with goat's cheese or feta became a restaurant menu fixture in the 1990s. It suits autumn and winter menus particularly well but works year-round.
